The equation is \(x = \sqrt{11 - 2x} + 4\). Isolate the square root: \(x - 4 = \sqrt{11 - 2x}\). The square root is defined only when \(11 - 2x \ge 0\), i.e., \(x \le \frac{11}{2} = 5.5\), and the right side is nonnegative, so \(x - 4 \ge 0\), i.e., \(x \ge 4\). Thus \(x \in [4, 5.5]\). Squaring both sides gives \((x - 4)^2 = 11 - 2x\), which simplifies to \(x^2 - 8x + 16 = 11 - 2x\), then \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\), factoring \((x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\), so \(x = 1\) or \(x = 5\). Only \(x = 5\) lies in the domain and satisfies the original equation (check: \(\sqrt{11 - 10} + 4 = 1 + 4 = 5\)). Thus the solution is \(x = 5\).

Answer: 5
